gemini.depth_why: The scenery in Barcelona is primarily urban and coastal, which remains visible and accessible throughout the year.
gemini.overview: Barcelona's scenery is defined by its urban landscape and Mediterranean coastline. The most famous views are of Antoni Gaudí's architecture, particularly the Sagrada Família and the city panorama from Park Güell. The setting includes the beaches along the coast and the backdrop of the Collserola hills.

blurbs.text: The city's urban views and coastal setting are visible. The panoramas from Park Güell and the hills provide a clear look at the grid of the Eixample district and the Mediterranean Sea beyond.

gemini.depth_why: The flat urban setting and river views remain accessible without seasonal closures.
gemini.overview: The primary views in the Argentine capital come from its setting along the wide Río de la Plata. Visitors look to the brightly painted houses of the La Boca neighborhood and the tree-lined avenues of Recoleta for visual appeal. The flat terrain provides modest riverfront walks and open park spaces.

blurbs.text: The wide, muddy waters of the Río de la Plata provide the main natural backdrop along the city's eastern edge. Inland, the visual appeal relies on the painted corrugated metal facades of the Caminito in La Boca and the shaded, monumental streets of Recoleta.
